title: (1) Pressure sensor
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 7 - (1) Pressure sensor] - 1) Check for failure by comparing the sensing pressure according to the high pressure/low pressure pressure sensor and the pressure gauge pressure. Turn on switches 1, 3, 5, 6 (High) and 2, 4, 5, 6 (Low) of the digital display select switch (SW1) as shown below, and the sensor pressure of the high pressure/low pressure sensors is displayed digitally by the light emitting diode LD1. **==> picture [145 x 51] intentionally omitted <==** **----- Start of picture text -----**

- 1 In the stopped condition, compare the pressure readings from the gauge and from the LD1 display. - (a) If the gauge pressure is 0~0.098MPa the internal pressure is dropping due to gas leakage. - (b) If the pressure according to the LD1 display is 0~0.098MPa there is faulty contact at the connector, or it is disconnected. Proceed to 4. - (c) If the pressure according to the LD1 display is 3.14MPa or higher, proceed to 3. - (d) If other than (a), (b) or (c), compare the pressure readings during operation. Proceed to 2. - 2 Compare the pressure readings from the gauge and from the LD1 display while in the running condition. - (a) If the difference between the two pressures is within 0.098MPa, both the affected pressure sensor and the main MAIN board are normal. - (b) If the difference between the two pressures exceeds 0.098MPa, the affected pressure sensor is faulty (deteriorating performance). - (c) If the pressure reading in the LD1 display does not change, the affected pressure sensor is faulty. - 3 Disconnect the pressure sensor from the MAIN board and check the pressure according to the LD1 display. (a) If the pressure is 0~0.098MPa on the LD1 display, the affected pressure sensor is faulty. - (b) If the pressure is 3.14MPa (in the case of the low pressure sensor, 0.98MPa) or higher, the MAIN board is faulty. - 4 Disconnect the pressure sensor from the MAIN board and short out the No. 2 and No. 3 pins of the connector (63HS, 63LS), then check the pressure by the LD1 display. - (a) If the pressure according to the LD1 display is 3.14MPa (in the case of the low pressure sensor, 0.98MPa) or higher, the affected pressure sensor is faulty. - (b) If other than (a), the MAIN board is faulty.

title: 1) In the case of SV1 (Bypass Valve)
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 7 - 1) In the case of SV1 (Bypass Valve)]
- (a) When the compressor starts, SV1 is ON for 4 minutes, so check operation by whether the solenoid valve is emitting an operating noise. 
- (b) Changes in the operating condition by solenoid valve operation can be confirmed by the temperature of the bypass circuit and the sound of the refrigerant.

title: 2) In the case of SV2 (Bypass)
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 7 - 2) In the case of SV2 (Bypass)]
- (a) SV2 goes ON in accordance with the rise in the high pressure in the cooling mode and heating mode, so check its operation by the LED display and the operating noise emitted by the solenoid valve. (Conditions during operation: See **Control of Heat Source Unit.** ) 
   - (b) Changes in the operating condition by solenoid valve operation can be confirmed by the temperature of the bypass circuit and the sound of the refrigerant. 
- 3) SV3~6, SV71~73 (Control of heat exchanger capacity) 
   - (a) Operations can be confirmed by LED display and operating sound of solenoid valve, because one or more of SV3~5, SV71 are turned on depending on conditions during cooling-only operations. 
   - (b) Operation can be confirmed by LED display and operating sound of solenoid valve, because all of SV3~5, SV73 are turned on during heating-only operations. 
   - (c) Operations can be confirmed by LED display and operating sound of solenoid valve, because one or more of SV3~6, SV71~73 are turned on depending on conditions during cooling-principal and heating-principal operations. 
–73–

title: Troubleshooting Steps
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 7 - Troubleshooting Steps]
1. **Check Pulse Signal Output**
   - Verify that the output phases φ1, φ2, φ3, and φ4 follow the sequence provided in the table.
2. **Valve Opening and Closing Operations**
   - Ensure that when power is turned on, a valve closing signal of 2,200 pulses is issued to position the valve at point A.
   - Confirm smooth operation with no sound or vibration from LEV. If not, check for any locking issues.
3. **Valve Opening Proportionality**
   - The valve opening should change in proportion to the number of pulses received by the stepping motor controlled by the microcomputer circuit board.
4. **Intermediate Connector and Circuit Board Connection**
   - Ensure that the intermediate connector is correctly connected on the outdoor unit.
   - Verify the connection points for both indoor and multi-board configurations as indicated (CN60, CNLV).
5. **Color Coding of Lead Wires**
   - Pay attention to the color coding of lead wires since they differ between intermediate connectors and circuit board side connectors.

title: Conclusion
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 7 - Conclusion]
- If the valve does not operate correctly or if there are issues with sound generation during operation, check the pulse signal output phases φ1 through φ4.
- Ensure that the valve is positioned at point A when power is turned on by issuing a 2,200 pulse valve closing signal.
- Verify smooth operation and absence of vibration or sound from LEV. If not, investigate for locking issues.
By following these steps, you can systematically troubleshoot and resolve any issues related to the BC controller and indoor unit's valve operations.

title: Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Procedure
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 1 - Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Procedure]
1. **Start**
   - Visually check for disconnection between connectors and terminals, and confirm correct lead colors.
2. **Intermediate Connector Check:**
   - Connectors:
     - Brown → 2
     - Red → 5
     - Blue → 1
     - Orange → 3
     - Yellow → 4
     - White → 6
3. **Visual Inspection:**
   - If disconnections are found, proceed to the next step.
   - If no disconnections are found:
     - Remove connectors from the board and use a tester to check conduction.
4. **Conduction Test:**
   - Check between connectors 1-3-5 and 2-4-6.
   - If conduction is OK, proceed to the next step.
   - If not:
     - Adjust or repair as necessary.
5. **Resistance Measurement:**
   - Use a tester to measure resistance between each coil (red-white, red-orange, brown-yellow, brown-blue).
   - Correct value should be 150Ω±10%.
6. **Resistance Test Results:**
   - If the measured resistance is within the specified range:
     - Proceed to the next step.
   - If not:
     - Change LEV.
7. **LEV Functionality Check:**
   - Check for the following:
     - LEV full open: ticking sound
     - LEV full closed: no sound
8. **Sound Test:**
   - If the sound test is OK, proceed to the next step.
   - If not:
     - Change LEV.
9. **LEV Full Closure Check:**
   - Confirm if LEV is fully closed.
   - If it is not fully closed:
     - Change LEV.
10. **LED Test:**
    - Attach check LEDs illustrated nearby to board connectors and confirm that LEDs light for 10 seconds.
    - Correct LED values should be as follows (assuming the illustration shows correct connections):
      - LED 6
      - LED 5
      - LED 4
      - LED 3
      - LED 2
      - LED 1
11. **LED Test Results:**
    - If LEDs light for 10 seconds:
      - Proceed to the next step.
    - If not:
      - Change the board.

title: Conclusion
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 1 - Conclusion]
- If all tests are successful, the process ends successfully.
- If any test fails, replace the LEV or the board as indicated.

title: Diagramma di Troubleshooting per la Valvola Solenoide
text:
[Documento: PQRY-P-YEM-A_SM-73-96.pdf | Sezione: 1 - Diagramma di Troubleshooting per la Valvola Solenoide]
1. **Inizio**
   - **Operazione OFF?**
     - **Sì:** Correggere il problema.
     - **No:**
       - **Verifica la connessione della valvola solenoide e lo stato del connettore (disconnessione o debolezza).**
         - **Sì:** Correggere il problema.
         - **No:**
           - **Operare il raffreddatore e il riscaldatore solo per il sistema refrigerante relativo alla valvola solenoide.**
             - **Nota 1:**
               - **Suono di clicking prodotto quando funzionante in tempo?**
                 - **Sì:** Rimuovere la bobina e verificare se c'è una forza magnetica.
                   - **Forza magnetica OK?**
                     - **Sì:** Verificare la differenza di temperatura tra l'entrata e l'uscita della valvola solenoide. Se la differenza è zero, la valvola è normale; altrimenti, è difettosa.
                       - **Valvola solenoide OK?**
                         - **Sì:** Valvola solenoide normale.
                         - **No:** Valvola solenoide difettosa.
                   - **No:**
                     - **Forza magnetica non presente.** Fermare l'unità e disconnettere il connettore della valvola solenoide dal pannello di controllo per verificare la conduttanza della bobina.
                       - **Conduttanza presente?**
                         - **Sì:** Con il connettore della valvola solenoide disconnesso, utilizzare un telecomando remoto per accendere l'unità e controllare l'uscita (220-240V) dal pannello di controllo.
                           - **Uscita 220-240V OK?**
                             - **Sì:** Cambiare il pannello di controllo.
                             - **No:** Cambiare la valvola solenoide.
                         - **No:**
                           - **Valvola solenoide difettosa.**
### Note:
1. **Nota 1:** Operare il raffreddatore e il riscaldatore solo per il sistema refrigerante relativo alla valvola solenoide.
2. **Nota 3:** Verificare la differenza di temperatura tra l'entrata e l'uscita della valvola solenoide. Se la differenza è zero, la valvola è normale; altrimenti, è difettosa.
